## Let Me Be Honest: That Was Impressive

Look, I'm not one to sugarcoat things, so when I tell you that going 3-1 yesterday was exactly what we should've done, believe it. A 75% accuracy rate isn't luck—it's reading the room better than everyone else. The Braves, Yankees, and Padres all came through exactly as predicted. And that one Astros loss? We'll get to that.

## The Astros Miss? A Coin Flip Gone Wrong

Here's the controversial take nobody wants to hear: that Astros pick at 50% confidence was basically a coin flip, and we knew it. When you're sitting at dead even probability, you're not making a prediction—you're making a gamble. Did it miss? Sure. Am I losing sleep over it? Absolutely not. The three wins with actual conviction behind them tell the real story.

## The Padres Pick Was Chef's Kiss

Can we talk about that Padres call at 63% confidence? That's the kind of pick that separates the amateurs from the pros. The Cubs never stood a chance, and we called it with authority. When you see those kinds of numbers, you don't second-guess—you ride the wave and collect your winnings.

## Tomorrow's Play: Braves Again? You're Damn Right

Here's where it gets interesting. We're going right back to the well with Atlanta. Phillies @ Braves, and we're taking the Braves at 61% confidence for the second straight day. Why? Because when something works, you don't overthink it.

Cristopher Sánchez on the mound for Philly against Tyler Mahle? The numbers favor Atlanta, and in this business, you follow the numbers until they prove you wrong. Yesterday they proved us right. Tomorrow? I'm betting on more of the same.

## The Hot Take You Need to Hear

Let me be provocative for a second: anyone who looks at a 3-1 day and focuses on the one loss is doing it wrong. That's loser mentality. Winners focus on the 75% accuracy and ask how to push it to 80%. The Braves delivered yesterday, the Padres crushed it, and the Yankees did their job. 

Tomorrow, we run it back with Atlanta. Same stadium, same confidence level, same expectation of results. If you're not on board, that's fine—but don't come crying when we cash another winner.

**Rico out. See you after the Braves handle business again.**
